content.comment_body: Why does the [product_name] analog module have two power input terminals (L+, M)? I connected a PT100 sensor to the module between M1+ and M2+, and also connected M1+ and IC1. I'm using a [product_name] controller, trying to read an analog value on AI3, but there's no change when I heat the PT100. Any suggestions?

Hello [user_name], all optional modules need to be powered using [product_name] power supply. The connector on the right side of the main unit is only for data transfer between the main controller and optional modules. Modules should be placed to the right of the main unit, and the connector must be properly inserted for communication.
Thank you everyone. The issues seem to be caused by a loose connection with the [product_name] module.

Hello [user_name]! Many expansion modules have L+ and M power terminals. You only need to connect one of them, as they are connected internally. This arrangement lets you daisy-chain power to the next expansion module more easily. Always make sure that your wiring is secure. For a PT100 (or PT1000 on updated modules), connect one wire to M1-, the second wire to M1+, and if there is a third wire, connect it to IC1. If your PT100 only has two wires, create a small bridge between M1+ and IC1. You can similarly connect a second PT100 on M2+, M2-, and IC2. Hope this clarifies things. Have a great day!
